newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Sodra says may raise pulp prices mid-April.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Sodra says may raise pulp prices mid-April.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Sodra said on Monday it might raise pulp prices in mid-April.
"In the middle of the month it could be on the agenda to announce price increases," Hans Burmeister, spokesman of Sodra's unit Sodra Cell, told Reuters.
"We can see that demand has picked up and that the delivery situation is better."
The move would follow North American pulp producers Georgia Pacific's and Stone Container's decisions to raise pulp prices as of May 1, he added.
Finnish forestry groups may follow suit, Finnish media reported on Monday.
It is, however, too early to say how large price increases should be, Burmeister said. Currently, long-fibre pulp costs about $520 per tonne.
"Stone has set $580 a tonne for long-fibre, so it should be around that level," Burmeister said.
Production halts in March and April have helped lower delivery volumes, which in turn increases the possibility to raise prices, Burmeister said.

At the end of this week or the beginning of next week North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) March pulp stocks figures are expected to be released, showing whether production halts have lowered inventory levels.
